Chunk a beagle file into partitions for processing.

get_chunks.Rd

Creates n chunks of a beagle file, where sequential lines are sent to different files round-robin style. Note that this is much faster on Linux than on Windows, since it avoids reading anything into memory using unix commands.

Usage

get_chunks(
  beagle_file,
  loci_per_chunk = 10000,
  max_read = 50000,
  outdir = dirname(beagle_file)
)

Arguments

beagle_file

path to .beagle or .beagle.gz file.

loci_per_chunk

numeric, default 10000. Number of loci to distribute to each chunk.

max_read

numeric, default 50000. Number of lines to read for splitting at once. Ignored on Linux.

outdir

path to output directory, default dirname(beagle_file) (the directory containing the input file).

Value

A vector of filenames for the chunks.

Author

William Hemstrom

Examples

# generate 100 SNP chunks
beagle <- system.file("extdata", "example.beagle.gz", package = "mechGEA")
chunks <- get_chunks(beagle, loci_per_chunk = 100)
#> Splitting into 15 files with approx. 100 snps per file.
file.remove(chunks) # remove the chunked files for the example only.
#>  [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
